issues.where: frames 118 to 122, then set-A-04.jpg frames 126 to 130: the base and the table around it
issues.what: the season change happens in the open over about 8 frames. The snow drift on the table is gone between 118 and 122. A bright warm flash lights the whole table at 126. The base jumps from iced winter wood, to a glowing gold version of the same base, to mossy spring rock by 130. All of this is plainly visible, not hidden inside the storm. At normal speed it reads as a flash and a swap.
issues.fix: spread the swap across the whole 102 to 138 window. Hide the base change behind the globe's motion and the snow storm (motion blur, the base turned away or out of the light), and morph the materials. Do not cut or flash. Remove the full-scene bloom.

issues.where: frames 114 to 122: glass versus base and background
issues.what: clean frames show two seasons at once. The glass turns pink and the background lights shift from blue to pink while the base still has winter icicles and the table still has its snow drift.
issues.fix: drive the glass tint, the background lights, the base and the surface dressing from one shared swap progress, so no frame shows parts from different seasons

issues.where: frames 126 to 138: the glass and the base
issues.what: in the winter to summer jump, the frost-white winter base glows gold at 126. At 132 the base is already sand with shells, but the glass is still a cold blue-grey wash with frost streaks and a dark winter-tree shape. The two halves are plainly from different seasons.
issues.fix: same as for spring: tie the glass interior, the frost on the rim and the base to one progress, and finish the interior change before the base shows its new material

issues.what: the spring petals on the table appear all at once and fully spread within 4 frames. In set-D-02.jpg the summer sand pile and the sand streak appear whole at 138, from nothing at 132. The surface is put down in one go rather than growing in.
issues.fix: grow the surface dressing after the landing: petals fall and gather over 0.5 to 1 s, and sand spills from the base as it lands. Keep the old snow fading out over the same span.

issues.where: frames 30 to 66 (the lift) and set-A-03.jpg 78 to 122 (the strokes)
issues.what: the globe hardly leaves the table. The bottom of the base stays at almost the same height while the globe drifts a little side to side and grows slightly toward the camera. The tilt is small and the strokes are small and even, so it reads as a gentle slide, not a heavy globe lifted with effort and shaken hard with sharp reversals.
issues.fix: give the lift clear height, with a short, effortful ease-in and a tilt that lags behind. Make the strokes unequal and larger, with hard stops at each reversal, so the base clearly moves off its spot and its reflection.

issues.what: the stir barely shows. The house, tree and few flakes look nearly the same from the press to the end. There is a slight haze but no visible whirl of particles that builds with the drag and dies away.
issues.fix: make the stir lift loose snow off the ground and turn it as one visible slow whirl around the scene, with streaks in the direction of the drag, then let it slow and fall over 2 to 3 s

issues.where: frames 30 to 62: the snow drift on the table under the base
issues.what: the snow drift on the table seems to keep its place under the base as the globe shifts, as if it were part of the base rather than lying on the surface
issues.fix: keep the surface snow fixed to the table and let the base move over it
